videos.title: Gemini 4 Argon Is Here (Fully Tested)
videos.ai_tech_id: Google Gemini 4 Argon (new frontier model, including Gemini Spark and the Antigravity coding/agent environment), benchmarked against Anthropic's Opus 5.5
summary: Paul J Lipsky puts Google's newly released Gemini 4 Argon through a hands-on test suite, covering model benchmarks, game generation inside Antigravity, app debugging, writing, the new Gemini Spark feature, and video/graphics editing.

He walks through each test case to show where Argon performs well versus where it struggles, then directly compares its output quality and behavior against Anthropic's Opus 5.5 to give viewers a practical sense of how the two frontier models stack up on real tasks rather than just benchmark charts.

The video closes with a verdict on Argon's overall capability and availability, framed as a sponsored segment for Hyperagent, and is aimed at viewers deciding which current-generation model to rely on for coding, writing, and creative work.

videos.title: Last 30 Days: your new real-time web search
videos.ai_tech_id: "Last 30 Days" (a free AI skill for real-time social/web research across YouTube transcripts, Reddit, Polymarket, Hacker News, and GitHub)
summary: Futurepedia introduces "Last 30 Days," a free AI skill positioned as a replacement for relying on stale, traditional web search when researching what people are currently discussing online.

Rather than pulling from a conventional search index, the tool scans recent YouTube transcripts, Reddit threads, Polymarket, Hacker News, and GitHub activity, then scores, filters, and synthesizes that raw activity into a short, digestible report of real-time sentiment and discussion.

The video frames this as a practical upgrade for anyone doing trend research, content ideation, or market/sentiment checks, since it surfaces what people are "actually saying right now" across multiple platforms in one synthesized pass instead of manual cross-platform searching.

videos.title: I Tested the Viral Reverse Engineer Anything Skill. What You Need to Know.
videos.ai_tech_id: "Reverse Engineer Anything" (REA) GitHub repo used as a Claude Code skill/workflow
summary: Nate Herk tests "Reverse Engineer Anything" (REA), a GitHub repo and accompanying Claude Code skill designed to help an AI agent rebuild features from existing apps by learning from concrete reference examples rather than vague instructions.

He demonstrates the approach by rebuilding features from his own Loom-inspired screen recorder, walking through a five-step REA workflow and explaining how giving Claude Code clear examples of desired output improves the quality of generated skills and workflows, while also flagging the limitations and edge cases he ran into during testing.

The video ends with his overall results and takeaways on REA's practical usefulness for AI agency builders and automation workflows, including links to the open-source repo and his own related free resources.

videos.title: 3 AI Prompts for Critical Thinking
videos.ai_tech_id: General-purpose AI chatbots (ChatGPT-style) used via targeted prompt engineering for fact-checking and critical thinking
summary: Sabrina Ramonov shares three prompts designed to counter the tendency to treat AI answers as proof, aimed at helping viewers question their own ideas and verify claims an AI model produces.

She details each prompt: asking the AI what it might be missing from an idea, asking it to provide data and sources for every claim so the viewer can independently verify them, and a keyword prompt called "SOCRATES" that has the AI probe the user's own understanding of a topic by having them answer from memory first.

The video is framed as a short, practical media-literacy exercise for anyone using AI tools like ChatGPT for research or learning, emphasizing checking cited sources directly rather than trusting AI-generated summaries at face value.

videos.title: Try This 5-Minute ChatGPT Reflection Prompt
videos.ai_tech_id: General-purpose AI chatbots (ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini) used via a structured positive-psychology reflection prompt
summary: Sabrina Ramonov presents a full, copy-ready prompt that turns ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini into a guided five-minute daily reflection exercise rooted in positive psychology, intended to train attention toward genuinely positive moments rather than generic AI flattery.

The prompt instructs the AI to ask one question at a time: identifying three specific good things from the day, exploring why each mattered, selecting a favorite moment to mentally relive for twenty seconds using sensory recall, and then naming what the user appreciates most about it, explicitly avoiding generic compliments or forced positivity.

The video closes the loop by having the AI help the user set an intention to notice one small good thing the next day, positioning the exercise as a lightweight, repeatable mental-health habit built entirely on prompt design rather than any specialized app or tool.

videos.title: Personal Agents, Clearly Explained
videos.ai_tech_id: Personal AI agents (Meta Muse, Dots, Grok Bot) versus DIY agents and a personal AI Workspace, compared against general chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini
summary: Jeff Su breaks down the spectrum of AI assistance available today, distinguishing plain chatbots (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) from do-it-yourself agents the user configures themselves, and from pre-built personal AI agents such as Meta's Muse, Dots, and Grok Bot.

He explains that the key difference between these tiers is how much the AI remembers about the user and how much setup work is required: personal agents are easier to start using out of the box, while a self-built AI Workspace with portable memory files gives the user more control and lets that memory move between different tools.

The video also addresses the privacy tradeoffs and ecosystem lock-in risks of committing to a vendor's personal-agent product versus maintaining an independent, tool-agnostic memory setup, closing with a recap to help viewers choose the right setup for their needs.
